senses.gloss:
sthūladhyāna
(‘gross meditation’)
------------------------------------------
Haṭhayogic works like the Gheraṇḍa Saṁhitā (6.2 to 14) describe this sthūla-ध्यान. It is meditation on the chosen deity in the heart.
The heart has to be imagined as a sea of nectar in which there is a beautiful island of precious stones, full of flowering and fruit-giving trees. In the midst of it there is a platform with a throne on which the deity is seated.
The form of the deity including the dress and the ornaments is also described in such works.

sthūlaśarīra
(‘the gross body’)
------------------------------------------
According to the Vedānta, the जीव or the individual सोउल्, is enveloped in three śarīras or bodies. They are: स्थूलशरीर (gross or physical body); सूक्ष्मशरीर (subtle body, also called लिङ्गशरीर); and, कारणशरीर (causal body).
The स्थूलशरीर is given by the parents and nourished by ड़ोओद्. It is subjected to ṣaḍvikāras or six changes viz., birth, existence, growth, change, decay and death.
Karma or the result of the actions of previous lives is an important factor in shaping this body.
See also KĀRAṆAŚARĪRA and LIṄGA-ŚARĪRA.
